translation.title: Ketoprofen Gel
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for pain relief and reduction of inflammation in degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis and tenosynovitis, peritendinitis, humeral epicondylitis (such as tennis elbow), muscle pain, and swelling and pain after injury.
translation.usage: Depending on your symptoms, apply an appropriate amount to the affected area - 1 to 4 times a day for the 3% gel, or 1 to 2 times a day for the 5% gel - and rub it in gently so that it is absorbed well.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, if you have experienced photosensitivity (skin reactions triggered by sunlight), if you have aspirin-induced asthma or have experienced it, if you are 6 months pregnant or more, or for children under 15. Do not use this medicine if you have experienced hypersensitivity to tiaprofenic acid, fenofibrate, bezafibrate, ciprofibrate or oxybenzone. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have bronchial asthma, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. While using this medicine and for 2 weeks after stopping it, avoid outdoor activities regardless of the weather; when you go out, cover the area where the medicine was applied with clothing, sunglasses, a hat, sunscreen or similar so that it is not exposed to ultraviolet light, and wear colored clothing, since white or thin clothing can let ultraviolet light through. Do not use it in the eyes or on mucous membranes. Using it on damaged skin or mucous membranes, or on areas with eczema or a rash, can cause temporary irritation and sharp pain, so use it with care. Do not use it on athlete's foot or ringworm. Do not use an occlusive (airtight) dressing over it. If your symptoms do not improve after about one week of use, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Adverse reactions may occur - rarely shock-like symptoms (hypersensitivity-like symptoms such as hives, difficulty breathing or facial swelling) or an asthma attack (dry crackles, wheezing, difficulty breathing), and occasionally contact dermatitis with redness, rash, itching, blisters, sores, irritation or swelling, dry skin and pigmentation, photosensitivity from direct sunlight, or a skin rash spreading over the whole body; if any of these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Store at room temperature and keep out of reach of children.
